open_points.subject: A01 caller-supplied computed identities
open_points.text: "A request that supplies one of these identities is refused."
open_points.question: Is this refusal only for create/author submissions (where the kernel must compute identity), or for any request field that contains these ids, including references to existing records (e.g., activate/run by flow_version_id)?
options: Refuse only when a create/author request tries to set the identity of the record being created
Refuse any request containing these identity fields, even as selectors
open_points.default_guess: Refuse only identity-supply on creation; allow ids when naming existing records.

open_points.subject: A04 trial-case port matching
open_points.text: "added only when its input values fit the contract version's input ports, its expected outputs, when present, fit the output ports"
open_points.question: Must trial-case inputs/expected_outputs be exact port sets (all required ports present, no extras), or are subsets allowed?
options: Require exact port set match (all declared ports, no unknown ports)
Allow subsets and treat missing ports as absent/implicit
open_points.default_guess: Require exact port sets with no extra names.

open_points.subject: A04 try implementation with unknown implementation id
open_points.text: "Trying an implementation ... executes an existing implementation ..."
open_points.question: What exactly happens when the requested implementation does not exist?
options: Treat as generic refusal under try operation
open_points.default_guess: Refuse as unknown reference before any execution.

open_points.subject: A05/M15 guard closed-set criterion
open_points.text: "its schema is a closed set" / "whose value schema is a closed set of values"
open_points.question: Which schema forms count as a 'closed set' for guard ports, and what equality semantics are used for matching guard values?
options: Only enum-like finite literal sets (e.g., JSON Schema enum), compared by canonical JSON value equality
Any schema that is semantically finite under the supported subset
open_points.default_guess: Treat only explicit finite literal sets (enum) as closed; compare by canonical JSON value equality.

open_points.subject: A10 approval coverage when request determinants change
open_points.text: "equal digests mean the same request, provided the instance's `api_base_url` is still the one the preview showed; after a restart that changed it, the approval no longer covers the send"
open_points.question: If other request determinants change (e.g., manifest required headers, credential header reference/value) while inputs and api_base_url stay the same, does the prior approval still cover the send?
options: Only api_base_url change invalidates approval; other determinants do not
Any determinant change of the outgoing request invalidates approval
Only binding-pinned determinants matter; instance/header changes ignored for coverage
open_points.default_guess: Follow text literally: invalidate on api_base_url change; otherwise keep approval coverage.

open_points.subject: A05 phase-9 reach check semantics
open_points.text: "at least one output of every function node reaches, through edges and nodes, a flow output or an operation node"
open_points.question: Is 'reaches' purely structural graph reachability, or must it account for guard conditions (and if so, how)?
options: Pure structural reachability ignoring guard values
Reachability only through at least one guard-satisfiable path
open_points.default_guess: Use structural reachability ignoring guard satisfiability.
